evidence.quote: A three-component multi-purpose PSD was designed. In line with previous cases, one PSD component of the PSD was designated to reduction and prefixation. To address the difficulties in stabilizing the dislocated largest medial fragment alongside smaller pieces, the upper PSD portion was equipped with four finger-like extensions along the entire posterior surface of the condylar head. The middle section of the PSD incorporated a large window for unobstructed visualization of the fracture line and its cranial ramifications. The lower PSD portion encompassed the neck region, reaching down to the level of the deepest point of the sigmoid notch.

items.name: Three-component multi-purpose patient-specific device (PSD)
items.finding: One component designated to reduction and prefixation; upper portion with four finger-like extensions along the posterior surface of the condylar head, middle section with a large window for visualization of the fracture line, lower portion encompassing the neck region down to the deepest point of the sigmoid notch

items.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: The upper PSD portion included six screw holes arranged in two rows (four along the common arch brace and one on each of the two central dome extensions) to ensure adequate fixation of the reassembled fragments, even if not every screw hole was occupied. The lower PSD portion contained three screw holes in a triangular configuration for anchoring to the condylar neck and base region.

items.finding: Upper portion six screw holes in two rows; lower portion three screw holes in a triangular configuration

evidence.quote: Its anterior border contained an undulating recess serving as docking site for the second PSD component, i.e. a “tandem” washer for load distribution and reinforcement of the LSFPSO.

The PSD “tandem” washer seated within the lateral recess along the first PSD component. This second PSD combined washer and navigation function: the tongue-in-groove design of the two components ensured accurate intraoperative transfer of the LSFPSO entry points onto the lateral fracture end at the ramus. Besides the two washer screw holes the PSD contained a third smaller hole for its temporary fixation during LSFPSO.

The lower PSD portion encompassed the neck region, reaching down to the level of the deepest point of the sigmoid notch.

The upper PSD portion included six screw holes arranged in two rows (four along the common arch brace and one on each of the two central dome extensions) to ensure adequate fixation of the reassembled fragments, even if not every screw hole was occupied. The lower PSD portion contained three screw holes in a triangular configuration for anchoring to the condylar neck and base region.
Its anterior border contained an undulating recess serving as docking site for the second PSD component, i.e. a “tandem” washer for load distribution and reinforcement of the LSFPSO.
